reader_message: What did Ines promise her brother, and does she start keeping it?

book_evidence.text: Before the ferry left, Ines took her brother's hand. “I will write to you every week,” she said, “even when there is nothing to tell.”
The ferry was still an hour from the far shore when Ines borrowed a pencil from the purser and began her first letter on the back of a timetable.

draft.reply: In Chapter 1, Ines promises her brother she will write to him every week, even when there is nothing to tell. In Chapter 2, she begins her first letter on the back of a timetable while the ferry is still an hour from the far shore. Together these moments show a promise kept faithfully from the very first day. What do you make of how quickly she starts?
